findings.rationale: 13-15% ambiguous swaps stated; harness gives 13.0% and 15.5% (single-phrase.txt L56-57).
Digest-word extraction described as the first d 11-bit groups of the hash; code masks each 16-bit big-endian group to its low 11 bits (Grid.lean L66).
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to match the code, or change the code and re-run all grid experiments.

findings.rationale: The 97.6% development figure has no evidence file anywhere in the repository.
findings.suggested_fix: Store the run that produced it under refs/experiments/ or drop the figure.

findings.rationale: Caption says joint decoding gains little for 2-of-3, but at 10% wrong words the gain is 40.7 to 61.2 (20.5 points).
findings.suggested_fix: Limit the statement to error rates up to 5%.

findings.rationale: 3-of-5 with exactly three cards at 3% is 79.0% in Table 2 and 83.2% in Table 4 (L489, L509): one condition, two samples, two headline numbers.
findings.suggested_fix: Say the two tables are independent runs of the same condition, or quote one.

findings.rationale: The 5-point confidence half-width holds for 400 trials only; Tables 1, 3 (k=6,8) and 4 use 200, 300 and 250 trials (6.9, 5.7, 6.2 points).
Prop. 1(a) and Eq. (3) ignore the header: a printed card satisfies the syndromes only with its unprinted header symbol appended (Grid.lean L86-89).
findings.suggested_fix: State the proposition for the header-extended codeword.

findings.rationale: RAID sentence: Patterson et al. 1988 covers RAID levels 1-5, not RAID-6, and it is the syndromes S0, S1 that correspond to P and Q (RS.lean L11-12), not the two parity words. Source not on disk.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite a RAID-6 source and say the first two syndromes are the P and Q checks.

findings.rationale: Step 5 says the secret row's syndromes are verified; the code runs the row decoder on it and fills unsettled columns from its parity (Grid.lean L329-340).
Claim that dictionary words resist transcription slips better than character strings is uncited.
Claim that no per-word error rates for handwritten word lists are published is unsupported.
SOUPS figures are correct, but the study measures recall from memory, not transcription, and the sentence does not say so.
Comment and reproducibility section point at grid-main-k4.txt, which is a header-only empty run; data are in grid-main-k4.final.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the .txt with the complete output.

findings.rationale: 'added a check to the secret' is a loose description of Tompa-Woll. Source not on disk.
blakley2007security dated 2007 (CRYPTO '84); krawczyk2007secret uncited and misdated.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix years; drop the uncited entry.

critical_flags.justification: Text says '24+2 leaves 13--15% of swaps ambiguous'. refs/experiments/single-phrase.txt L56-57 (24+2, parity only) gives 13.0% ambiguous for an adjacent swap and 15.5% for a swap of any two words (84.5% unique). The upper end is 15.5, not 15.

Paper defines digest words as 'the first d 11-bit groups of SHA-256(...)'. Parity39/Grid.lean L62-66 takes word i as ((h[2i] << 8) | h[2i+1]) & 0x7ff, the low 11 bits of the i-th 16-bit big-endian group. For d = 2 the paper's rule reads hash bits 0-21 and the code reads bits 5-15 and 21-31, so an implementation written from the paper is incompatible with the tool that produced every grid result.
